title: “And how, monks, is a monk one who does not bind up the wound? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye,…
content: “And how, monks, is a monk one who does not bind up the wound? Here, monks, when a monk sees a form with the eye, he grasps the general feature, grasps the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise—he does not restrain that cause, does not guard the eye, does not practice restraint of the eye. When he hears a sound with the ear … smells an odor with the nose … tastes a flavor with the tongue … feels a touch with the body … cognizes a phenomenon with the mind, he grasps the general feature, grasps the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the mind faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise—he does not restrain that cause, does not guard the mind, does not practice restraint of the mind. Thus, monks, is a monk who does not bind up the wound.”

title: “Householder, suppose there is a pit of glowing embers, deeper than a man’s height, filled with glowing embers that are neither flaming nor smoking. Then…
content: “Householder, suppose there is a pit of glowing embers, deeper than a man’s height, filled with glowing embers that are neither flaming nor smoking. Then a man comes who desires to live, not to die, who desires happiness and loathes suffering. Two strong men grab him by both arms and drag him toward that pit of embers. What do you think, householder? Would that man twist his body this way and that?” “Yes, venerable sir. Why is that? Because he knows: ‘If I fall into this pit of embers, I will thereby meet death or deadly suffering.’” “So too, householder, a noble disciple reflects: ‘The Blessed One has said that sensual pleasures are like a pit of embers — of much suffering, much despair, and the peril is even greater.’ Having seen this as it actually is with perfect wisdom … he cultivates such equanimity.”

title: “One who in this world has abandoned sensuality, Left home, gone forth, With sensual desire and existence destroyed — Him I call a brahmin.” “One…
content:
“One who in this world has abandoned sensuality,
Left home, gone forth,
With sensual desire and existence destroyed —
Him I call a brahmin.”

“One who in this world has abandoned craving,
Left home, gone forth,
With craving and existence destroyed —
Him I call a brahmin.”

“Having abandoned the human yoke,
Transcended the heavenly yoke,
Free from all bondage —
Him I call a brahmin.”

“Having abandoned liking and disliking,
Cool, free from attachments,
A hero who conquers all worlds,
Who subdues all —
Him I call a brahmin.”

title: Standing to one side, the deity Subrahmā recited this verse to the Blessed One: This mind is always afraid, This mind is always agitated, What…
content:
Standing to one side, the deity Subrahmā recited this verse to the Blessed One:
This mind is always afraid,
This mind is always agitated,
What is wished does not arise,
What is not wished does arise.
If there is a way to be without fear,
Please tell me what I ask.

(The Blessed One):
Apart from enlightenment and austerity,
Apart from sense restraint,
Apart from abandoning all —
I see these things
That lead to safety
For all beings.

title: Elder Parāpariya: The eye goes to forms — Without restraint, without checking, Not seeing the danger, That person does not escape suffering. The ear goes…
content:
Elder Parāpariya:

The eye goes to forms —
Without restraint, without checking,
Not seeing the danger,
That person does not escape suffering.

The ear goes to sounds —
Without restraint, without checking,
Not seeing the danger,
That person does not escape suffering.

Not seeing the escape,
Enjoying odors,
That person does not escape suffering,
Because of lust for smells.

Remembering sweet and sour as supreme,
Remembering bitter as supreme,
Enslaved by the taste of craving,
The mind cannot awaken.

Remembering contacts —
Beautiful and pleasurable —
Infatuated, conditioned by lust,
One meets many sufferings.

The mind toward all these things —
All five —
If unable to guard them,
Suffering follows that person.

title: “Monks, misconduct in sensual pleasures, when performed, developed, and cultivated, leads to hell, to the animal realm, to the realm of hungry ghosts. The very…
content: “Monks, misconduct in sensual pleasures, when performed, developed, and cultivated, leads to hell, to the animal realm, to the realm of hungry ghosts. The very least result of misconduct in sensual pleasures is being born human with enmity from adversaries.”

title: “‘For life, the arahants have abandoned unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. Today, this night and day,…
content: “‘For life, the arahants have abandoned unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. Today, this night and day, I too abandon unchastity, live the holy life, live secluded, abstaining from sexual intercourse, the low practice. In this factor, I follow the arahants and will observe the uposatha day.’ This is the third factor attained.”

title: “Monks, then I thought: ‘This Dhamma I have attained is deep, hard to see, hard to realize, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of mere logic,…
content: “Monks, then I thought: ‘This Dhamma I have attained is deep, hard to see, hard to realize, peaceful, sublime, beyond the scope of mere logic, subtle, to be understood only by the wise. But this generation delights in sensual pleasures, is devoted to sensual pleasures, is fond of sensual pleasures. For a generation that delights, is devoted, and is fond of sensual pleasures, it is hard to see this principle of specific conditionality (dependent origination); it is also hard to see the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all substrates, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.’”

title: “One who here has overcome sensual desires, Craving so hard to overcome in the world, Sorrowless, without longing, Has cut the stream, unbound. Dry up…
content:
“One who here has overcome sensual desires,
Craving so hard to overcome in the world,
Sorrowless, without longing,
Has cut the stream, unbound.

Dry up what is before,
Let there be nothing after —
If you grasp nothing in between,
You will live at peace.

For one who has no ‘mine’
In name-and-form at all,
Who grieves not for what is not,
Suffers no loss in the world.

For whom there is no ‘this is mine,’
Nor ‘this belongs to another,’
Finding nothing that is self,
He does not grieve at ‘I have nothing.’

Not harsh, not greedy,
Without desire, always the same —
When asked, I speak about
The benefit of the unshaken.

The one who has known without lust,
He has no inclinations —
Freed, not striving,
He sees security everywhere.

The sage does not speak
Of being equal, worse, or better —
Peaceful, without stinginess,
He neither takes nor rejects.” So spoke the Blessed One.

title: “And what, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives without restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is defiled by forms cognizable by the…
content: “And what, monks, is dwelling heedfully? If one lives without restraint of the eye faculty, monks, his mind is defiled by forms cognizable by the eye. For one with a defiled mind, there is no gladness. Without gladness, there is no rapture. Without rapture, there is no tranquility. Without tranquility, suffering remains. For one who is suffering, the mind does not become concentrated. When the mind is not concentrated, phenomena are not clearly seen. When phenomena are not clearly seen, he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully’ … the ear faculty … the nose faculty … the tongue faculty … the body faculty … If one lives without restraint of the mind faculty, his mind is defiled by phenomena cognizable by the mind. For one with a defiled mind, there is no gladness … he is called ‘one who dwells heedfully.’ Thus, monks, is dwelling heedfully.”
